Growing Minds. Igniting Dreams. Empowering Futures.
Welcome to our school
Growing Minds. Igniting Dreams. Empowering Futures.
Leopold Primary School is a vibrant, two-site, multicultural, primary school based in the heart of North-West London. Our main site, located on Hawkshead Road, is a two form entry provision with nursery. Our second site is Leopold Gwenneth Rickus, which is a one form entry primary school from Year 1 to Year 6.
Equity for all is crucial to the growing success of the school. Both sites have an excellent team of staff who dedicate themselves to meeting the needs of all children. Our curriculum is designed to engage all learners, inspire excellence and is personalised to meet the needs of all our community.
As a multicultural school, we celebrate the rich diversity of our community. We value the different backgrounds, languages and experiences that our families bring, and we work in partnership with parents and carers to support every child's learning journey.
Visit Us
We warmly welcome prospective families to visit both of our sites to see our school in action. Please contact our main office to arrange a visit and discover how Leopold Primary School could be the perfect place for your child to learn and grow.

pageCache.pageTitle: Leopold Primary School - Executive Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Executive Headteacher's Welcome
Growing Minds. Igniting Dreams. Empowering Futures.
Welcome to the new Leopold Primary School website.
We are one school and one community over two sites in the London Borough of Brent. We are highly aspirational for the future of our children.
Our vision for our children is:
'We strive for ambitious, articulate pupils who can problem solve, communicate confidently, show resilience, and act with kindness'
Our curriculum is ambitious and carefully crafted to ensure that this vision is realised. With this in mind, we ensure that all children have a wide variety of learning experiences both in and out of school. The school is well resourced so that learning is enhanced. Parents are the children's first teachers so parental engagement is integral to the work of the school. All members of the Leopold community are committed to the school vision including ensuring equity of opportunity and the highest of standards.
The future is very bright for the continuing success of Leopold Primary School. I am proud to have the privilege of being part of such a wonderful community.
Interim Executive Headteacher

About Us
Leopold Primary School is a vibrant, two-site, multicultural, primary school based in the heart of North-West London. Our main site, located on Hawkshead Road, is a two form entry provision with nursery. Our second site is Leopold Gwenneth Rickus, which is a one form entry primary school from Year 1 to Year 6. Both sites have their own Head of School to lead and manage the operational aspects of the site and share an Executive Headteacher with strategic responsibility.
Equity for all is crucial to the growing success of the school. Both sites have an excellent team of staff who dedicate themselves to meeting the needs of all children. Our curriculum is designed to engage all learners, inspire excellence and is personalised to meet the needs of all our community.
As a multicultural school, we celebrate the rich diversity of our community. We value the different backgrounds, languages and experiences that our families bring, and we work in partnership with parents and carers to support every child's learning journey.
Growing minds. Igniting dreams. Empowering futures.

pageCache.pageTitle: Leopold Primary School - Vision and Aims
pageCache.text:
Vision and Aims
Our School Vision
"We strive for ambitious, articulate pupils who can problem solve, communicate confidently, show resilience and act with kindness"
Our Aims
Growing Minds
We cultivate a love of learning where every child develops the knowledge, skills, and understanding they need to succeed. Through a rich, ambitious curriculum and high-quality teaching, we encourage children to think critically, ask questions, and embrace challenges. We believe that every mind has the potential to grow, and we provide the support and opportunities for all our pupils to flourish academically, socially, and emotionally.
Igniting Dreams
We inspire our children to dream big and believe in themselves. By celebrating each child's unique talents and interests, we create an environment where aspirations are encouraged and achievements are recognised. We expose our pupils to a wide range of experiences and possibilities, helping them discover their passions and develop the confidence to pursue their goals, no matter how ambitious.
Empowering Futures
We equip our children with the resilience, independence, and values they need to become responsible, active citizens. Through fostering strong character, promoting respect and equality, and building partnerships with families and our community, we prepare our pupils not just for the next stage of their education, but for life. We empower them to make positive contributions to the world around them and to shape their own successful futures.
Our approach to positive behaviour for learning and for life
At Leopold Primary School, we aim to create a calm, safe and happy environment where exemplary behaviour enables all pupils and adults to feel secure, respected and ready to learn. Everyone in our school community is expected to maintain high standards of conduct, to take responsibility for their behaviour and to encourage others to do the same.
We recognise that every child is unique and at a different stage of social, emotional and behavioural development. Only through a consistent, calm and fair approach to supporting behaviour will we be able to create an environment in which children can learn, develop positive relationships and grow into responsible, resilient individuals.
We believe that behaviour is a form of communication. Children do well when they can, and when they struggle, it is our responsibility as adults to teach, guide and support them back to success. Our approach is rooted in the principle that when adults change, everything changes.
At Leopold Primary School:
Behaviour is learned and can be taught
Certainty beats severity
Relationships are the foundation of good behaviour
Every child deserves dignity, safety and belonging
Children are never defined by their behaviour
Mistakes are expected and planned for
Repair matters more than punishment
Adults lead with calm, consistency and compassion

pageCache.text:
Attendance
At Leopold Primary School, we expect all children on roll to attend every day, when the school is in session, as long as they are fit and healthy enough to do so. There is a proven connection between success at school and high attendance. We do all we can to encourage the children to attend, and to put in place appropriate procedures if attendance is poor. We believe that the most important factor in promoting good attendance is the development of positive attitudes towards school. To this end, we strive to make our school a happy and rewarding experience for all children. We will reward children whose attendance is very good. We will also make the best provision we can for those children who, for whatever reason, are prevented from coming to school.
2026/27 WHOLE SCHOOL ATTENDANCE TARGET 96%
Celebrating Good Attendance
All children who have 100% attendance will receive an excellence certificate for attendance, awarded in assembly each term.
We celebrate the class who has the highest attendance each week with a special certificate and a reward for gaining 100% attendance over a week.
Letters of reognition are sent home if children improve their attendance over the year. These are usually children who have been monitored and their parents/ carers have been attending attendance meetings with the School Attendance Officer (SAO).
Term-time Leave
The school has adopted the policy of all requests for leave in term-time to be submitted to the Head of School or the Executive Head. Leave will not be approved unless it is under proven exceptional circumstances and in these cases further evidence will be requested.
The Head of School or Executive Head may request a meeting with parents/ carers to discuss the request and/or documentation may be required to back up a request. Any unauthorised extended leave or holidays taken in term-time will result in a referral to the School Attendance Officer and a penalty notice/ fine. The Local Authority authorises the fine that is sent to families.
Punctuality
Learning at Leopold Primary School starts from 8.45am therefore getting to school on time is essential. Punctuality is a life skill. Parents/ carers are expected to support their children with this.
To support children being in school and arriving on time, the school does the following:
This means it would be an exceptional circumstance to be late rather than a regular occurrence.
The school gates close at 8.45am. Children arriving after this are considered 'Leopold late' as school starts at 8.45am. The register is taken and lessons begin.

SEND
Inclusion is at the heart of everything we do at Leopold Primary School. School staff and leaders work together to ensure pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) are identified early and supported through high quality teaching and additional interventions. This support is outlined in our SEND Information Report.
Our SEND provision is overseen by a Special Educational Needs Coordinator(SENCo), Kaitlyn Atkins, who works across both the Hawkshead Road and Gwenneth Rickus sites. For any queries regarding SEND at Leopold, please email sen@leopold.brent.sch.uk.
Please click on the Brent Local Offer for support and information that is offered in the Brent Community.
